rows.q: What is our replenishment policy for high-risk inventory?
rows.message: This is a SAMPLE policy written for the DSports AI proof of concept. The planning target is a 95% cycle service level. Safety stock covers demand uncertainty over the supplier lead time and is calculated from forecast error. The reorder point is the forecast demand over the lead time plus the safety stock. Stock is reviewed weekly, and the recommended quantity brings the inventory position up to the forecast demand over the lead time and review period plus the safety stock. Quantities are rounded up to the supplier's case pack and raised to the minimum order quantity.

rows.q: What is the minimum order quantity for our suppliers?
rows.message: This is a SAMPLE document written for the DSports AI proof of concept. For products priced below ₹5,000, the Minimum Order Quantity (MOQ) is 6, 12, 24, or 48 units, and they ship in case packs of 6. For bats, bicycles, and premium shoes, the MOQ is 2, 4, or 6 units with no case pack. The replenishment recommendation always rounds up to the exact MOQ and case pack held in the inventory master data. A purchase order quantity is raised to the MOQ even if the calculated need is smaller, then rounded up to a whole number of case packs. If an open purchase order will arrive after the projected stock-out date, the buyer asks the supplier to expedite it before raising a new order. (Source: Supplier Lead Times and MOQ)

rows.q: What is the clearance policy for inventory older than 90 days?

Stock with at least 180 days of cover is high overstock. Critical aging stock is older than 120 days and has at least 150 days of cover. A clearance discount up to 50% can be proposed by merchandising. Discounts above 50% need approval from the Head of Merchandising and the Finance controller. rows.message: I can model discounts from 1% to 70%. 80% is outside that range, so I haven't calculated anything. Tell me a discount between 1% and 70%, for example 30% or 50%.

rows.q: Which of those is better?
rows.message:
This data is POC synthetic. No single discount for all 3 products keeps every product above the 10% margin floor; 30% and 50% discounts break it for at least one product. Discounting only 1 of the 3 products at its individual best discount gives a net benefit of ₹815.

A 0% discount is forecast to sell 61.8 units, generating ₹130,820 revenue and ₹52,416 margin. A 30% discount is forecast to sell 116.7 units, generating ₹165,541 revenue and ₹21,851 margin, with a net benefit of ₹9,157. A 50% discount is forecast to sell 215.8 units, generating ₹209,544 revenue and a negative margin of ₹-48,452, with a net benefit of ₹8,515.
